name: Spike wallbounce: a superbounce out of a window in a spiked wall face
techNote: WJ_DS. A wall (face x 380, top y 600) whose face carries 19-thick spike strips (layer 6, spikeScript) below y 40 and from y 110 up, leaving a plain window at y 40-110. The dot falls at it from x 300, y 74 with no jumps left (wallJumpsLeft -1, airJumpsLeft 0: the superbounce-wall lab's start) and dashes flat into the window with the jump buffered 1 frame in (dashJump 1): the airborne wall touch ends the dash and the dash boost bounces it off (SpecialWallJump(0.6, ...): Velocity (-276, 703), momentum.y 401, facing turned from the wall). The bounce's first tick lifts the hurtbox's top past y 110 while its front edge is still in the upper strip (tick 5, spike3 *0: OnTriggerEnter2D, free), and 5.5 u/tick away from the wall plus the facing flip (the hurtbox turns to x-25..x+15) clear it by the next tick: one tick brushed, inside graceFrames 1. The bounce is the only way up (no ground, no jumps) to the finish box above. Ghosts: drift (stick held to the wall once the bounce's lock ends: back into the spiked face on ticks 16-18, dies), no-jump (the same dash without the buffered jump: no bounce, the dot stays in the window).

ghosts.label: Spike wallbounce: superbounce, brushes the spikes above for 1 tick
Stick back to the wall after the bounce: into the spiked face
Dash with no buffered jump: no bounce, stays in the window
